messages:
Taylor: Heads-up: We need to re-evaluate the MVP cutlist for embeddings cache pilot. Customer feedback suggests embedding latency is more critical than previously scoped features. Can we shift slices?
Maya: What specifically are they asking?
Taylor: They want embeddings cache warmed per-tenant for pilot, and a simple TTL-backed cache API so prewarm + fast responses for repeated queries. No fancy eviction policies needed for MVP.
Priya: We have a milestone freeze 2024-07-10. Any changes need a clear rollback.
Kevin: Engineering estimate: add TTL cache + per-tenant namespace + prewarm hook is ~1.5 dev-weeks if we reuse existing cache infra. If we also need precompute pipelines, that's extra.
Jordan: Ops note: cache prewarm will increase staging load during canary. Need to throttle prewarm.
Maya: Proposal: Move non-critical admin UX and monitoring enhancements to v1, prioritize embeddings cache API and prewarm for MVP.
Taylor: Customer agrees to no self-serve UI in MVP as long as cache delivers p95 latency < 30ms.
Priya: Commercial asks that we add a milestone check: pilot will be measured only against latency SLAs, not feature completeness.
Kevin: Cutlist MVP: include: per-tenant cache namespace, TTL API, prewarm endpoint (ops-driven), basic hit/miss metrics. Exclude: eviction tuning, tiered storage, cache dashboard.
Jordan: Rollout plan: staging canary with synthetic prewarm -> pilot tenants -> monitor 72h -> expand. Rollback: disable prewarm and fall back to warm-on-read.
Maya: Risk register: cold start spikes during prewarm -> mitigation: staggered prewarm + traffic shaping; namespace collision -> mitigation: tenant isolation checks.
Taylor: Decision: accept cache-first MVP slice, bump monitoring + UX to v1. Owners: Kevin infra (owner), Maya product cutlist (owner), Jordan ops (canary owner), Priya legal/comms (customer note).
release-bot: Canary scheduled: 2024-07-05 03:00 UTC (staging).
Priya: I'll update milestone board and customer note.
Kevin: Will prioritize the cache PR and share flag doc.
Maya: I'll publish a short runbook for prewarm ops.
Taylor: Thanks team, closing this thread. :rocket:
